title: The Bay of Pigs Disaster
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss the 1961 Bay of Pigs Invasion, a CIA-backed attempt by Cuban exiles (Brigade 2506) to topple Fidel Castro. They cover the Cold War context (Soviet ties, Eisenhower's domino theory), the CIA's recruitment and training in Florida and Guatemala, the flawed plan that Kennedy repeatedly scaled back (smaller, night landing, different site), the New York Times leak, the air strikes and the half-strength second strike, the coral reef landing problems, the failed air cover that involved American Alabama Air National Guard pilots shot down (Thomas Willard Ray), the capture of over a thousand exiles, and their 1962 trade for food and medical aid. The episode closes with a listener mail about a listener's LSD experience while listening to the show.
topics: Jim Wasserman Rasenberger book The Brilliant Disaster

segments.title: Opening banter and background on Batista and Castro
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open by framing the Bay of Pigs as a case study in bad decisions. They discuss Batista, Castro's takeover of Cuba on New Year's Day 1959, the early US relationship with Castro, and the Soviet Union's rising influence.

segments.title: Cold War motives and the CIA plan
segments.summary: The hosts explain US fear of communism in Latin America, Eisenhower's domino theory, and the CIA's plan to remove Castro through a covert operation made to look like a Cuban uprising. Training Cuban dissidents was chosen because direct US invasion was illegal.

segments.title: Recruiting and training exiles
segments.summary: Recruits were drawn from Cuban exiles in Miami, with training first in the Everglades and later in Guatemala. The CIA posed as a company, and the hosts note that the training was an open secret among exiles.

segments.title: Brigade 2506 and Kennedy's approval
segments.summary: The exile force is named Brigade 2506 after Carlos Rafael Santana, a comrade killed in training. Kennedy, who had campaigned as tough on communism, is briefed on the plan, which relies on a hoped-for uprising in Cuba and air strikes on Castro's air force.

segments.title: Kennedy scales back the plan
segments.summary: Kennedy requests a smaller operation, a different landing site near the Bay of Pigs far from the mountains, and a night landing. The CIA objects but no one backs out. Planning failures are discussed, including misread reconnaissance showing coral as seaweed.

segments.title: Air strikes, leaks, and the landing day
segments.summary: A New York Times story exposes the operation and Kennedy publicly denies US involvement. Only half of Castro's planes are destroyed in the first air strike, and Kennedy refuses a second. On landing day the supply ships run aground on coral and are struck by Castro's air force; the Rio Escondido explodes.

segments.title: Failed air cover, Ray's death, and the prisoner exchange
segments.summary: Air cover arrives an hour early due to a time zone error and is shot down. The pilots were American Alabama Air National Guard members, including Thomas Willard Ray, whose death the US denied until the 1990s. Over a thousand exiles were captured and later traded for food and medical aid negotiated by James B. Donovan.

segments.title: Aftermath and legacy
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how the failure strengthened Castro and pushed Cuba toward the Soviet Union, damaged Kennedy's image, and is linked to later US escalation in Vietnam. They recommend reading Jim Rasenberger's book The Brilliant Disaster.

segments.title: Listener mail: LSD trip
segments.summary: A listener named Mike describes listening to the show during an LSD trip and thanks the hosts. The hosts also mention the email address for listener mail.
